Below you are told what you can see and hear around you right now. Say what you do from now on: how you move, chosen from the ACTIONS below.
The passage has two long walls, the blue wall and the yellow wall. They are the same two walls for everyone here, so where people are and which way anyone moves is told by these walls.
Other people see how you move, if you are in their view. Nobody else knows your intent or your reason.
You may be asked again later, if something changes.

HOW TO REPLY
Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"intent": what you are trying to do, in your own words.
"action": the one action you choose (see ACTIONS), written exactly as it is named there.
"reason": why, in your own words. Nobody else sees it.
The format, with placeholders: {"intent": "<what you are trying to do>", "action": "<the name of one action>", "reason": "<why>"}

ACTIONS
Choose one of these. You do it from now on, until it is done or you choose again. Write its name exactly as it is given in quotes.
"carry on": keep walking along the line you are on, at your usual speed.
"slow down a little": keep walking along your line, a little slower than your usual speed, until the person you would meet has passed you.
"slow down a lot": keep walking along your line, much slower than your usual speed, until the person you would meet has passed you.
"stop and wait": stand still for a moment. Then you walk on along your line, unless you are asked again.
"step a little towards the blue wall": move a little over towards the blue wall as you walk, then walk on along that new line.
"step a little towards the yellow wall": move a little over towards the yellow wall as you walk, then walk on along that new line.
"step well towards the blue wall": move well over towards the blue wall as you walk, unless the wall stops you sooner, then walk on along that new line.
"step well towards the yellow wall": move well over towards the yellow wall as you walk, unless the wall stops you sooner, then walk on along that new line.
"step back": walk backwards a short way. Then you walk on along your line, unless you are asked again.

ABOUT YOU
- You are 25 years old.
- You are a woman.
- You are on your way to the supermarket.
- You are walking at 1.30 m/s. Your usual walking speed is 1.30 m/s.
- The fastest you can walk is 2.00 m/s.
- Your body is 0.50 m wide.
- You are Indian.
- You are easy-going and tend to give way.
- You live in Singapore.

WHERE YOU ARE
- You are in a passage 1.75 m wide, between the blue wall and the yellow wall. You are 1.45 m from the blue wall and 0.30 m from the yellow wall.
- It is busy and noisy around you.
- It is the middle of the day.

WHO YOU CAN SEE
- Person 1, 4.8 m away, ahead of you, 0.87 m from the blue wall.
  They are walking at 1.30 m/s, in the opposite direction to you, and the distance between you is shrinking.
  Their body is 0.70 m wide.
  They look about 25 years old.
  They look like a man.
  They look Indian.
  They are pulling a large suitcase.
  You do not find them especially attractive.
  You have never seen them before.

WHAT YOU HAVE DONE SO FAR
- 2.0 s ago you decided: "I'll shift a bit toward the yellow wall to give the man with the suitcase room to pass, since the passage is narrow."
  Since then you have moved 0.6 m over towards the yellow wall.
  You have finished that.
- 1.0 s ago you decided: "Keep giving the man with the suitcase room to pass by staying close to the yellow wall as I walk on."
  Since then you have moved 0.1 m over towards the yellow wall.
  You have finished that.

At your current speeds you would meet Person 1 in about 1.8 s.

Something has changed since you last decided. What do you do now? Your choice replaces whatever is left of your earlier one. Reply with the JSON object only.

{"intent": "Keep to the yellow-wall side so the man with the suitcase can pass, staying on my line without crowding him.", "action": "carry on", "reason": "I'm already close to the yellow wall and have given plenty of room; at 1.8 s to meet there's no need to change course or speed, and staying predictable is easiest for both of us in the busy passage."}

Stepping out of the role now. Earlier, as this person, you:
- decided: "I'll shift a bit toward the yellow wall to give the man with the suitcase room to pass, since the passage is narrow."
  You chose: "step a little towards the yellow wall".
- decided: "Keep giving the man with the suitcase room to pass by staying close to the yellow wall as I walk on."
  You chose: "step a little towards the yellow wall".
- decided: "Keep to the yellow-wall side so the man with the suitcase can pass, staying on my line without crowding him."
  You chose: "carry on".
Was what you did based on anything: a law or official guidance, a published study, a local custom, a habit, or nothing in particular? If you know a specific source, name it. If there is none, say so. That is a perfectly good answer.

If you moved to one side, why that side and not the other? It may have been a custom or rule about which side to keep to, where the other person was, which side had more room, something the other person did, or nothing: either side would have done as well. That is a perfectly good answer too.

HOW TO REPLY
Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys:
"basis": in your own words, what you did was based on.
"kind": one of "law_or_guidance", "published_study", "local_custom", "habit", "common_sense" or "none".
"source": a specific source you know of, as a citation, or "none".
"applies_to": which of your decisions this is about.
"side_basis": why you moved to that side and not the other: one of "custom_or_rule", "where_they_were", "more_room", "what_they_did", "either_side" or "did_not_move_aside".
"side_detail": in your own words, why that side.
The format, with placeholders: {"basis": "<what it was based on>", "kind": "<one of the kinds>", "source": "<a citation, or none>", "applies_to": "<which decision>", "side_basis": "<one of the side reasons>", "side_detail": "<why that side>"}
